title: Critical Discourse Analysis: Fairclough
short_description: Guidance for analyzing text, discursive practice, and social practice with attention to ideology, hegemony, and intertextuality.

phases.title: Text analysis
phases.description: Analyze lexical choices, grammar, modality, agency, nominalization, passivization, and presupposition.
prompts: What textual choices carry evaluative meaning?

phases.title: Discursive practice
phases.description: Analyze production, circulation, consumption, genre, and intertextual relations.
prompts: Which prior texts or discourses are invoked?
recommended_actions: Link discourse features to actors and codes.

phases.title: Social practice
phases.description: Connect discourse to wider social relations, institutions, ideology, and hegemony.
prompts: What alternative is made difficult to say?
How does the text relate to wider social practice?

concepts.description: The presence or transformation of other texts and discourses within a text.
prompts: Which text or discourse is echoed?

concepts.description: Degrees of certainty, obligation, possibility, or necessity expressed in language.
prompts: What is presented as only possible?

concepts.description: Turning processes into nouns, often obscuring agency.
prompts: What action is turned into a thing?

concepts.description: Passive constructions that can background actors or responsibility.
Background assumptions treated as already accepted.
prompts: What must be accepted for this sentence to make sense?

concepts.description: A figurative mapping that frames one domain through another.
prompts: What does the metaphor hide or highlight?

concepts.description: Discursive work that makes an action, actor, or policy appear justified or necessary.
prompts: Which authority, value, or necessity is invoked?

concepts.description: Meaning systems that help reproduce social relations and power.
Dominance secured through consent, common sense, and institutional practice.

sources.apa: Fairclough, N. (1992). Discourse and social change. Polity.
sources.note: Use for text, discursive practice, social practice, and intertextuality.

sources.apa: Fairclough, N. (1995). Critical discourse analysis: The critical study of language. Longman.
sources.note: Use for textual analysis, ideology, and power.

sources.apa: Chouliaraki, L., & Fairclough, N. (1999). Discourse in late modernity: Rethinking critical discourse analysis. Edinburgh University Press.
sources.note: Use for linking CDA to social theory and late modernity.
